newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BCE wheat futures drop, further falls seen.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BCE wheat futures drop, further falls seen.

text.p: Wheat futures finished lower on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Wednesday and traders said a bleak export outlook will have a further depressing effect.
"Both wheat and flour exports will be extremely limited and a large surplus will eventually hit the market," said Istvan Grebats of Termin Broker.
Milling wheat prices for January 1997 dropped by 280 forints to end at 27,940, while March and May 1997 contracts went down by 400 forints each to end at 28,600 and 29,020 respectively.
"With hog prices at a low (of 185 to 190 forints) breeders are looking for the cheapest feed possible. Maize prices are still way below wheat prices," Grebats said.
Feed wheat prices for March and May 1997 also dropped by 400 forints to close at 27,800 and 27,900.
Maize futures, although relatively steady at the moment, are also likely to slip from January, he said.
Maize remained steady on Wednesday for all but the July 1997 maturity which closed at 21,500 forints, down 100.
Total grains futures turnover was a below-average 417.4 million forints or 750 lots, of which 655 were milling wheat.
(Lot size 20,000 kgs for all contracts. $=163.28 forints) --Denes Albert, Budapest newsroom +36 1 327 4040
